tools.name: studio_status
tools.title: Get the status of the studio
tools.description: Gives the state of the agent server: the profile, the active mod, the revision, the undo and redo steps, the tool groups and the limits. This tool changes nothing. Call it first.

host.description: editor for the agent server of the editor, headless for oltool mcp serve.

profile.description: The name of the open profile, or none while no profile is open.

mods.description: The ids of the mods of the profile, in load order.

active_mod.description: The id of the mod that gets the edits, or none.

tier.description: The tier of the active mod: 1 for data only, 2 for the OpenLancer runtime.

targets.description: The ids of the target games of the active mod, for example vanilla-1.1.

can_edit.description: True when the host takes edits now. When it is false, reason tells why.

reason.description: Why the host takes no edits now, or none.

dirty.description: True when the session has edits that it did not save.

rev.description: The revision of the edit view, as text. Each edit, undo and redo increases it. A save does not change it.

origin.description: Who made the step: user, agent or recovery.

undo.description: The step that Undo takes back, or none.

origin.description: Who made the step: user, agent or recovery.

redo.description: The step that Redo does again, or none.

system.description: The system: reference of the system that the Scene shows, or none.

mission.description: The msn: reference of the mission script that the editor shows, or none.

cutscene.description: The thn: reference of the cutscene that the editor shows, or none.

view.description: What the editor shows now, or none in the host without a window.

paused.description: True while the user pauses the edits of the agent.

tool_groups.description: The tool groups that the user shows. A tool of another group gives not_available.

list_rows.description: The rows of a page when the call gives no limit.

max_list_rows.description: The largest limit of one page.

result_kilobytes.description: The most text of one result, in KB. A larger result gives the error limit.

calls_per_second.description: The most calls that the server takes in one second.

wait_seconds.description: How long a call waits while the user edits, in seconds. Then it gives busy.

tail_seconds.description: How long the second part of a call can run, for example a target check, in seconds.

render_pixels.description: The most pixels on each side of an image of render_scene and render_cutscene. A larger panel of capture_panel gives a smaller image.

edit_items.description: The most items that one call of delete_items or duplicate_items names.

edit_sections.description: The most sections that one edit call changes, adds or removes.

batch_steps.description: The most steps of one edit_batch call.

code.description: The kind of the error. Each kind has a fixed meaning, for example not_found or invalid_argument.

detail.description: The detail code of the error, for example ReferenceNotFound or BadArgument.

message.description: What is wrong and how to correct it.

index.description: The index of the step of a batch that failed, or none.

target.description: The reference or the text that the error is about, or none.

field.description: The argument or the field that the error is about, or none.

step_code.description: For the error step_failed: the code of the error of the step, for example not_found. Else none.

anyOf.description: A result of the tool. The structured content of a call is a result or a tool error.
A tool error. The call has isError true. Read the message, then correct the call.

tools.name: mission_dry_run
tools.title: Dry run a mission
tools.description: Runs the trigger rules of the retail game on one mission script, step by step, without a game world. You give the inputs. An input starts the mission, loads a checkpoint, starts at a trigger, runs an active trigger or says that an event happens. It can also set a fact or the place of the player, or advance the time in heartbeats of 1/30 s. The result gives each step with its changes in the order of the game, and the state after the last step. The query keeps no state, so send all inputs at each call. This tool changes nothing.

script.description: The reference of a mission script, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini.

inputs.description: The inputs in order, at most 1000, with at most 108000 heartbeats in all. Each input is an object with a kind. The kinds are start_mission, load_checkpoint {trigger}, start_at {trigger}, run_trigger {trigger}, event {line} and fact {line, on}. The other kinds are heartbeats {count} or {until_timer: true}, player_system {system} and player_in_space {value}. A trigger is a trg: reference. A line is {key, values} with the value names of describe_mission_name. A value that the line does not give matches any value. When it matches two waiting lines, the line whose values it gives in full is the event. Else the call gives invalid_argument. start_mission, load_checkpoint and start_at start a new run and remove the inputs before them. start_at starts the triggers that wait at a trigger, as a play from that trigger does. The fact and player inputs before them stay, in their net form.
